1_sitz.summary: This 1964 Beatles love song sits in the Neotechnic phase (MUMFORD-NEOTECHNIC ~1900-pre-1945) that made electric-guitar-based popular music possible, extended into the post-1945 mass-media era. MODEL-KNOWLEDGE: the specific proximate conditions — postwar Anglo-American youth culture, the transistor radio + 7-inch vinyl + television broadcast infrastructure (Ed Sullivan Feb 1964), and the emergence of an affluent teenage consumer demographic — are the material substrate for the song's romantic-lyric idiom and its global circulation. The song's simple first-person love-declaration presupposes a secular, individualist courtship regime (no arranged-marriage frame, no religious authority) characteristic of MODEL-KNOWLEDGE: post-1960 Western sexual-cultural liberalization.
1_sitz.tradition: Anglophone popular music (British Invasion / early Beatles romantic ballad)

3_frame_axes.evidence_quote: First-person avowal: 'I give her all my love / That's all I do'; 'I know this love of mine / Will never die' — knowledge grounded in personal declaration.
'The kiss my lover brings / She brings to me' — bodily/relational act as ground of the claim.
Adoring, exalting register — the beloved as one who 'gives me everything'; love figured as cosmic and imperishable ('Will never die').
Wholly positive, protective framing of the beloved; no shadow admitted.
The lovers' bond is figured as participating in a cosmic order (stars/sky) that guarantees its permanence.
No explicit account of how an ultimate relates to world; the 'world' at stake is the dyad itself.
Takes the love at face-value and gathers it into an enduring, cosmically-framed whole ('A love like ours / Could never die'); no suspicion or deconstruction.
Plain first-person avowal with minimal figuration outside the closing star/sky couplet.
'And if you saw my love / You'd love her too' — inferring a general conclusion (anyone would love her) from the singular case of the beloved's qualities.
'Bright are the stars that shine / Dark is the sky / I know this love of mine / Will never die' — cosmic imagery mapped onto the endurance of love.
Reality of the love depends on the you-and-I bond: 'A love like ours / Could never die / As long as I / Have you near me.'
'She gives me everything' — the beloved is a personal agent who gives, brings, is near.
Fulfillment is mutual presence and exchange: 'She gives me everything'; 'As long as I / Have you near me.'
'I give her all my love / That's all I do' — the whole vocation is devoted self-giving to the beloved.

4_moves.line_paraphrase: The singer transfers the entirety of his affection to the beloved.
The singer characterizes that giving as the whole of his activity — nothing else fills his doing.
The singer entertains a counterfactual in which the addressee lays eyes on the beloved.
In the same counterfactual the addressee, once having seen her, would also come into love for her.
Dropping the hypothetical, the singer affirms his own factual love for her.
The beloved reciprocates in kind, handing over the totality of what she has to the singer.
A particular gesture of hers — a kiss — arrives from her to him, and it arrives with tenderness.
The singer once more affirms his love for her, after her reciprocation has been narrated.
The singer predicates permanence of the shared love — it is of a kind that could not perish.
The permanence is conditioned: it holds while the singer keeps the addressee close to him.
The singer sets the scene by attributing brightness to the shining stars.
In the same scene the singer attributes darkness to the sky.
The singer claims epistemic access — he asserts that he knows a proposition about the love.
The embedded proposition itself: this particular love of the singer's does not perish.
The singer closes with a final affirmation of his love for her.

6_gaps.gap_description: The passage of TIME — the duration across which the love must last — is presupposed by the QUD but never given a scale, a horizon, or an occasion. The permanence claims float free of any timeline.
6_gaps.interest_reason: 'Will it last?' has no answer without a 'how long'; the poem's refusal to name a temporal horizon is itself the interpretive opening.

6_gaps.gap_description: How is it warranted that ANY hypothetical seer would also love her? The universal claim about her lovability rests on the singer's own loving as its only evidence.
6_gaps.interest_reason: The circle (I love her → anyone who saw her would love her → therefore my loving is warranted) is the classic lover's fallacy and invites commentary on projection vs. perception.

6_gaps.gap_description: How does the singer come to KNOW (not merely hope or promise) that his love will not die? The epistemic verb is used but no source of the knowledge is offered.
6_gaps.interest_reason: This is the QUD's crux: 'will it last?' answered by 'I know.' A commentator will press on what could ground first-person knowledge of a future affective state.

6_gaps.gap_description: Why are the brightness of the stars and the darkness of the sky named at all? Their relation to the love-claim is left implicit — analogy? condition? oath-formula? cosmic witness?
6_gaps.interest_reason: The cosmological images are the poem's most interpretable hinge; commentary lives on whether they function as duration ('as long as'), as guarantor, or as mere backdrop.

6_gaps.gap_description: The beloved's own account of the kiss — her intention, her feeling, why 'tenderly' — is absent. She acts but does not speak.
6_gaps.interest_reason: The whole poem is spoken ABOUT her; the form structurally silences her side, and later readers (feminist, dialogical, midrashic) characteristically step in exactly here.

6_gaps.gap_description: What follows FROM keeping her near? The proximity is willed but no consequence — comfort, growth, protection, union — is named.
6_gaps.interest_reason: A minor gap; the wish stands as its own end, and few commentators would press it.

6_gaps.gap_description: What is the extension of 'all my love' — is it exhaustive of the singer as a person, of his affections generally, or only of his romantic capacity?
6_gaps.interest_reason: M2's totalization answers the degree question inside the text; not a rich site for later commentary.

6_gaps.gap_description: How is it known that a love 'like ours' could never die? The endurance is asserted counterfactually with no test, no comparison class, no mechanism.
6_gaps.interest_reason: M13 supplies a propositional attitude ('I know') but not a ground — so a commentator will feel the warrant is still open even after M13 answers 'how do you claim it?'

6_gaps.gap_description: How does the singer know that his entire activity reduces to the giving in M1? The totalizing self-report is asserted without any check — no witness, no test, no counter-instance considered.
6_gaps.interest_reason: The move stakes everything on a first-person totalization; a commentator naturally asks whether the lover can be trusted about the whole of his own activity.

6_gaps.gap_description: WHY does the singer love her? No quality, deed, history, or cause of the love is given — the loving is posited as a bare standing state.
6_gaps.interest_reason: The QUD asks whether the love is real; a love with no stated ground is exactly what a later reader wants to interrogate, and the form (declaration, not account) forecloses an answer from within.

6_gaps.gap_description: Does she give everything BECAUSE he gave everything (M1), or independently? The text places the two totalized gifts side by side without saying whether they are exchange, echo, or coincidence.
6_gaps.interest_reason: Whether M1↔M6 is contractual reciprocity, mimetic mirroring, or free parallel gift is a live question a commentator would want to name.

6_gaps.gap_description: No THIRD party, community, witness, or world outside the dyad is admitted; the love is sealed off from any social, familial, or normative context that could test or sustain it.
6_gaps.interest_reason: The lyric form excludes the outside; commentary that reads love as socially embedded will want to open exactly this seal.

6_gaps.gap_description: Only 'this love of MINE' is declared imperishable; her love's endurance is not asserted. The permanence claim is one-sided.
6_gaps.interest_reason: The form (first-person avowal) can only vouch for the speaker's side; a reader who takes the QUD seriously will notice that half of 'will it last?' is structurally unanswered.
